subject: English
passage: Urban planners around the world are working to address air pollution and public health challenges in cities, and in many cases, solutions that incorporate natural systems or processes can help tackle such problems. In response to deteriorating air quality in downtown areas, the city of Portland partnered with the environmental group Green Cities Initiative to expand urban tree canopy coverage throughout the central business district. The increased tree coverage creates natural air filtration and cooling zones that reduce pollution levels and urban heat, thus promoting improved public health outcomes.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Nature-based solutions can be effective ways to achieve urban planning goals.
choices.B: A partnership between Portland and Green Cities Initiative shows the importance of collaborative approaches to improving urban environments.
choices.C: As indicated by a recent project, urban tree coverage helps reduce air pollution and heat in city centers.
choices.D: City planners now recognize that nature-based urban solutions provide better long-term outcomes for public health than solutions that are not nature-based do.

explanation:
Choice A is the best answer because it best states the main idea of the text: that nature-based solutions can be effective for achieving urban planning goals. The text indicates that in many cases where planners are trying to address urban challenges, their methods incorporate natural systems or processes. The text then gives an example of this phenomenon, a project in Portland that expanded tree coverage in the downtown area, creating natural filtration and cooling that improves public health.

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. There is no evidence in the text to support a direct comparison of the efficacy of nature-based urban solutions to other types of solutions. The text merely indicates that nature-based approaches can often be effective.
